newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natgas firms in busy trade, summer softe.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natgas firms in busy trade, summer softe.

text.p: UK natural gas market saw a slew of slightly firmer deals for day-ahead gas on Thursday but the rest of the forward curve was thinly traded and a touch softer.
At least 400,000 therms traded on day-ahead gas, with prices reaching a high of 10.20 pence a therm (p/th).
"It seems to be being bid up which seems to suggest there was a system buy," said one dealers said.
But traders could not confirm whether or not there had been trade on the flexibility mechanism.

Transco expected temperatures to fall slightly below seasonal norms on Friday to 8.9 degreess Celsius, after several days of mild weather. But consumption was forecast to be just 47 percent of peak day demand nevertheless.
A few deals were also seen on the summer months at softer levels than on Wednesday when the third quarter market was heavily bought by a single trader.
May, June and August all traded at 10.20 p/th, shedding about 0.10 p/th on Wednesday's values.
"It looks like those summer requirements have been covered," said one dealer. "We're getting the summer doldrums and it's only April."
Winter gas was untraded on the physical market after January and February 1998 each edged very slightly lower on the IPE market but held around the mid-16 level.
